Despite numerous discussions about this topic, the answers were not clear and I don't want to necropost. So here goes, please don't hate me if it seems obvious to you.
In available text codes:
\{          Increases the text size by one step.
\}          Decreases the text size by one step.
Apparently.
However:
1. does this permanently change the text size or only for that particular Show Text?
2. what if you just want to change the
line height
separately from the text size?
Well, there was this old solution which seemed sort of like on the right track:
Otherwise, you can copy the default function:
Click to expand...
Code:
Window_Base.prototype.standardPadding = function() {
    return 18;
};
Click to expand...
paste into a text file, save it as a *.js, and include it as a plugin. Then you change that number in there.
Click to expand...
Need help with vertical text alignment
Hello everyone! I'm currently working on a personal project and i've been trying to get the OMORI font to work with RPGMaker, it looks fine on menus but on messages the text height looks misaligned compared to the original Gamefont Font  [/SPOILER]  I have tried lowering the line height but that...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
However, this apparently changes all padding and not specifically Y-position of text lines (i.e.; line height). Since it appears CSS-like code may work(?) am I correct in assuming there is something like this available?
Code:
Window_Base.prototype.lineHeight = function() {
    return 36;
};
Thanks for any tips/hints in this matter.

You can take the code that utunnels provided, paste it into a text editor, save as a *.js file and include as a plugin. Change the number 36 to the number of pixels you want.
You should also be able to do this with some number of already-made plugins, such as Yanfly's Core Engine.
unikadas said:
Since it appears CSS-like code may work(?)
Click to expand...
RPG Maker MV and MZ use JavaScript.

Thank you so much! I have now had time to
actually
run RPGMaker MV and try a bunch of things.
Here's what I found out and what readers should know:
1. I've used VS_SFont to make a nice pixel perfect graphic font. Then GALV's Message Styles which sets a fontSize parameter; setting this once (such as to size 14 for my squatty font) makes everything beautiful. Once. Gamewide. But so much for dynamic changing! Because using \{ and \} on the first line treats the Show Text command as default first, then all following smaller text on the same line doesn't matter. So commands like Show Text:
\}\}\}Trying
to lay out second line
and 3rd line height \^
Results in displays like:
Code:
Trying

and 3rd line height
If I disable both of these and play around with plugins, the results are like this:
2. \{ and \} still produce the first-line oddity.
3.
Code:
Window_Base.prototype.standardPadding = function() {
    return 14;
};
appears to do nothing.
4.
Code:
Window_Message.prototype.lineHeight = function() {
   return 14;
};
appears to do nothing. (Whereas
with
GALV's Message Styles plugin activated it seems to cut lines of text in half. Maybe is this because of what
utunnels
said in post #4 that it doesn't actually change y position and it conflicts with GALV's text handling?)
5. Using the code from post #4 (
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/line-height-of-text.173147/post-1480988
) appears to do nothing. With or without plugins activated.
6. Using the code from post #6 (
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/line-height-of-text.173147/post-1481167
) appears to do nothing. With or without plugins activated.
So I guess there's either another plugin somehow messing with things preventing those post #4 and #6 from doing anything. Here is my list of plugins at the moment. The last one is the code from post #6 which I'm turning on and off to play with things.
Conclusion:
This is unsolved. GALV's Message Styles controls line height beautifully, but only for one universal font that cannot dynamically switch. I may have to dig in and attempt to modify the plugin if that's allowed (can't remember, have to check if that's ok with GALV's distribution parameters).
Also, I find it strange that \{ and \} generally are causing the first line to always have a different line height even if every displayed character is smaller than default. Anyone else notice this in their games?

The code not working was simply a misplaced closing bracket - I've corrected it above.
As a tip, when code/a plugin isn't working as expected, a first troubleshooting step should be to press F8 and go to the Console tab - you would've seen an error was preventing the plugin from being loaded.
